name: Curated third-party API change alerts for a niche vertical
buyer: Engineering lead or agency running integrations against several partner APIs in a vertical such as payments, logistics, EHR, tax or shipping
pain: Integrations break and the team learns about it from a customer; raw commit emails on large specs bury the real changes.
wedge: Curate 30-50 vertical APIs that generic tools ignore (e.g. healthcare, tax or shipping vendors) and send per-field, severity-classified alerts at a flat $19/mo for 10 watched APIs.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: Flat self-serve $19/mo with pre-curated vertical API coverage built from public specs and changelogs, automated via diffing pipelines.
scan1Edge.falsifier: Free oasdiff-based tools and free tiers like FlareCanary cover the same need; if target buyers don't pay $19/mo for curated coverage over free tools, the edge fails.
scan1Edge.unit: USD per month for monitoring ~10 APIs

substitutesNoted.name: Generic page monitors (PageCrawl) / vendor RSS / GitHub emails

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: ESTIMATE from research notes: ~90% margin. Price taken from an idea-site suggestion, not observed purchases. Churn is expected to be high since a user may need an alert only once.

majorUncertainty: Whether anyone pays for curated coverage given free substitutes and no evidence of payment for manual versions.
unknowns: Whether any buyer pays for this (no payment evidence found)
Which verticals have enough un-served API vendors
FlareCanary free-tier details are only in research notes (excerpt did not show it)
Search demand rated 'Low' by one idea site (not in cited excerpt)
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Scraping vendor changelogs may breach vendor terms of service. Many vendors publish no OpenAPI spec.
